item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03480","case1_error":"Treats four total overtime hours as four hours per day, multiplying overtime pay by five.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final total 4600 after correctly writing (60 × 8 × 14) + 2500, which equals 9220.","reason":"The first incorrectly repeats overtime across days; the second supplies an incorrect final number after a correct formula.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03481","case1_error":"Uses current fuel as total required capacity, then subtracts only the truck's current fuel.","case2_error":"Assigns the brother's lifting capacity to Felix, omitting the conversion to Felix's weight and lifting multiplier.","reason":"The first constructs an incorrect fill-up relation; the second substitutes another person's lifting capacity for the requested person's capacity.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03482","case1_error":"Explicitly evaluates 80 − 16 as 40 instead of 64.","case2_error":"Supplies unsupported final answer 55 after correctly expressing the sick animals as (26 + 40 + 34) / 2.","reason":"The first shows a specific arithmetic evaluation error; the second gives an incorrect final number without showing an erroneous evaluation step.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03483","case1_error":"Evaluates 48 − 17 − 10 as 11 instead of 21, propagating the incorrect remainder into profit.","case2_error":"Evaluates 34 − 8 − 9 as 27 instead of 17.","reason":"Both explicitly miscalculate correctly written subtraction expressions.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J03484","case1_error":"Treats the brother's entire pre-candy balance as Michael's gift, then answers Michael's initial money instead of the brother's.","case2_error":"Sets feeding cost equal to purchase cost, ignoring the stated 20% increase.","reason":"The first conflates a balance with a transfer and answers for the wrong person; the second omits a required cost increase.","judgment":"different"}]}
